title: Address to Marcianus: one path of faith
english: I know, beloved Marcianus, your zeal for the piety that is toward God — the only road that leads a human being unto life everlasting. ([[life everlasting >> Bible:Jn 3:16]]; [[Mt 19:16 >> Bible:Mt 19:16]]) So I share your joy, and I pray that by keeping the faith whole and unshaken you may be well-pleasing to God who made you. ([[well-pleasing to God >> Bible:Heb 11:6]])

Would that it were granted us to be always together, to help one another, and to lighten the labors of this present life by daily converse on what is profitable! But since at this moment we are parted in body, we will not omit — so far as we are able — to speak with you a little by writing, and to set out briefly the preaching of the truth, for the confirming of your faith. ([[confirming of your faith >> Bible:Lk 22:32]]; [[Acts 16:5 >> Bible:Acts 16:5]])

We send you, as it were, a memorandum of the chief points, that from a little you may reach much: that in a short compass you may grasp the whole body of the truth, and in few words receive the demonstration of the things of God. So it will bear fruit for your own salvation, and you will put to shame all who teach what is false, and with all confidence you will hand on our healthy and pure teaching to everyone who wishes to learn it. ([[healthy teaching >> Bible:1 Tim 1:10]]; [[Tt 1:9 >> Bible:Tt 1:9]]; [[Tt 2:1 >> Bible:Tt 2:1]])

For there is one way that leads upward for all who see, lit with heavenly light; but many and dark and contrary are the ways of those who do not see. This way leads to the kingdom of heaven, joining the human being to God; but those ways bring down to death, separating the human being from God. ([[kingdom of heaven >> Bible:Mt 7:13-14]]; [[Jn 14:6 >> Bible:Jn 14:6]])

Therefore it is necessary for you and for all who care for their own salvation to make your course unswerving, firm, and sure by means of faith, lest you grow slack and be held back among bodily desires, or turn aside and wander from the straight.
notes_covered: one illuminated way vs many dark ways
translator_notes: Copy-text: Armenian PO XII.5 (PDF locked). Readable sense-check: Barthoulot French (PD). Pass B independent of Robinson 1920 / Wilson English.
Inline Logos bible refs on quotes/allusions ([[display >> Bible:…]]).

title: Holiness of body and soul; Psalm 1 triad
english: Now since the human being is a living creature compounded of soul and flesh, it is necessary to take account of both. And since offenses arise from both sides, holiness of the flesh is restraining abstinence from every shameful thing and every unjust deed, and holiness of the soul is keeping faith toward God entire — neither adding to it nor taking from it. ([[neither add nor take away >> Bible:Dt 4:2]]; [[Rev 22:18-19 >> Bible:Rev 22:18-19]])

For piety toward God is withered and stained by the defilement of the flesh, and it is broken and polluted and no longer whole if falsehood enters the soul. But it will keep its own beauty and measure when truth abides in the soul and purity in the flesh.

For what profit is it to know the truth in words, and to pollute the flesh and work the works of evil? Or what profit can purity of the flesh bring, if truth is not in the soul? For these rejoice with one another, and are allied, to set the human being face to face against God.

Therefore the Holy Spirit says through David: ‘Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]) — that is, the counsel of the nations that do not know God; for those are ungodly who do not worship the God who truly is. And therefore the Word says to Moses: ‘I am the One who is.’ ([[Ex 3:14 >> Bible:Ex 3:14]]) But those who do not worship the God who is — these are the ungodly.

‘And has not stood in the way of sinners’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]): but sinners are those who have knowledge of God and do not keep his commandments — that is, disdainful scorners. ‘And has not sat in the seat of the pestilent’ ([[Ps 1:1 >> Bible:Ps 1:1]]): now the pestilent are those who by wicked and perverse teachings corrupt not only themselves but others also. For a seat is a symbol of teaching. Such then are all heretics: they sit in the seats of the pestilent, and those who receive from them drink in the venom of their doctrine.
translator_notes: Standard §2 = French numbered 1 in Barthoulot. Independent English; Robinson/Wilson check-only.

title: Rule of faith; baptism into Father, Son, Spirit
english: But we shall not suffer anything of this kind if we hold the rule of the faith without deviation, and do the commandments of God, believing in God and fearing him as Lord and loving him as Father. Now this doing is produced by faith; for Isaiah says: ‘If you do not believe, neither shall you understand.’ ([[Isa 7:9 >> Bible:Isa 7:9]] LXX sense)

And faith is produced by the truth; for faith rests on things that truly are. For in things that are, as they are, we believe; and believing in things that are, as they ever are, we keep firm our confidence in them. Since then faith is the preservation of our salvation, we must bestow much care on maintaining it, that we may have a true comprehension of the things that are.

Now faith occasions this for us, even as the elders, the disciples of the apostles, have handed down to us. First of all it bids us bear in mind that we have received baptism for the remission of sins, in the name of God the Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who became incarnate and died and rose again, and in the Holy Spirit of God. ([[baptism … name >> Bible:Mt 28:19]]; [[Acts 2:38 >> Bible:Acts 2:38]]; [[remission of sins >> Bible:Lk 24:47]])

And that this baptism is the seal of eternal life, and is the new birth unto God, that we should no longer be sons of mortal men only, but of the eternal and everlasting God; ([[new birth >> Bible:Jn 3:3-5]]; [[Tt 3:5 >> Bible:Tt 3:5]]) and that what is everlasting and continuing is made God; and is over all things that are made, and all things are put under him; ([[all things under him >> Bible:1 Cor 15:27]]; [[Ps 8:6 >> Bible:Ps 8:6]]) and all the things that are put under him are made his own; for God is not ruler and Lord over the things of another, but over his own; and all things are God’s; and therefore God is Almighty, and all things are of God.
translator_notes: French §3 block; baptismal triad explicit. Independent English.

title: One unmade Father who makes what was not
english: For it is necessary that things that are made should have the beginning of their making from some great cause; and the beginning of all things is God. For he himself was not made by any, and by him all things were made. ([[all things were made through him >> Bible:Jn 1:3]]; [[Col 1:16 >> Bible:Col 1:16]]; [[Heb 1:2 >> Bible:Heb 1:2]])

And therefore it is right first of all to believe that there is One God, the Father, who made and fashioned all things, and made what was not that it should be, and who, containing all things, alone is uncontained. ([[made what was not >> Bible:Rom 4:17]]; [[2 Macc 7:28 >> Bible:2 Macc 7:28]])
Now among all things is this world of ours, and in the world is the human being: so then this world also was formed by God.
translator_notes: Standard §4; French marker 4. in PO. Independent English.

title: Word and Spirit: creation, adornment, Pauline triad
english: Thus then there is shown forth One God, the Father, not made, invisible, creator of all things; above whom there is no other God, and after whom there is no other God. ([[no other God >> Bible:Isa 45:5]]; [[Dt 4:35 >> Bible:Dt 4:35]]; [[Dt 6:4 >> Bible:Dt 6:4]])

And since God is rational, therefore by the Word he created the things that were made; and God is Spirit, and by the Spirit he adorned all things: as also the prophet says: ‘By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by his spirit all their power.’ ([[Ps 33:6 >> Bible:Ps 33:6]])

Since then the Word establishes — that is, gives body and grants the reality of being — and the Spirit gives order and form to the diversity of the powers, rightly and fittingly is the Word called the Son, and the Spirit the Wisdom of God.

Well also does Paul his apostle say: ‘One God, the Father, who is over all and through all and in us all.’ ([[Eph 4:6 >> Bible:Eph 4:6]]) For over all is the Father; and through all is the Son, for through him all things were made by the Father; and in us all is the Spirit, who cries ‘Abba, Father,’ ([[Rom 8:15 >> Bible:Rom 8:15]]; [[Gal 4:6 >> Bible:Gal 4:6]]) and fashions the human being into the likeness of God. ([[likeness of God >> Bible:Gen 1:26]])

Now the Spirit shows forth the Word, and therefore the prophets announced the Son of God; and the Word utters the Spirit, and therefore is himself the announcer of the prophets, and leads and draws the human being to the Father.
translator_notes: Independent English from French sense-check of Armenian.

title: Three points of the rule: Father, Word, Spirit
english: This then is the order of the rule of our faith, and the foundation of the building, and the stability of our way of life: God, the Father, not made, not material, invisible; one God, the creator of all things: this is the first point of our faith.

The second point is: the Word of God, Son of God, Christ Jesus our Lord, who was manifested to the prophets according to the form of their prophesying and according to the method of the Father’s economy; through whom all things were made; who also at the end of the times, to complete and gather up all things, was made man among men, visible and tangible, in order to abolish death and show forth life and produce a community of union between God and man. ([[gather up all things >> Bible:Eph 1:10]]; [[abolish death >> Bible:2 Tim 1:10]]; [[Heb 2:14 >> Bible:Heb 2:14]])

And the third point is: the Holy Spirit, through whom the prophets prophesied, and the fathers learned the things of God, and the righteous were led forth into the way of righteousness; and who in the end of the times was poured out in a new way upon humankind in all the earth, renewing the human being unto God. ([[poured out >> Bible:Joel 2:28]]; [[Acts 2:17 >> Bible:Acts 2:17]]; [[Tt 3:5 >> Bible:Tt 3:5]])
translator_notes: Independent English; prior Robinson English not copied.

title: Baptismal regeneration through the three; knowledge of Father via Son and Spirit
english: And for this reason the baptism of our regeneration proceeds through these three points: God the Father bestowing on us regeneration through his Son by the Holy Spirit. For as many as carry the Spirit of God are led to the Word, that is to the Son; and the Son brings them to the Father; and the Father causes them to possess incorruption. ([[led by the Spirit >> Bible:Rom 8:14]]; [[incorruption >> Bible:1 Cor 15:53-54]])

Without the Spirit it is not possible to behold the Word of God, nor without the Son can any draw near to the Father: for the knowledge of the Father is the Son, and the knowledge of the Son of God is through the Holy Spirit; and, according to the good pleasure of the Father, the Son ministers and dispenses the Spirit to whomsoever the Father wills and as he wills. ([[no one comes to the Father except through me >> Bible:Jn 14:6]]; [[Mt 11:27 >> Bible:Mt 11:27]])

title: Father as Most High for believers, Jews, Gentiles; judgment
english: And by the Spirit the Father is called Most High and Almighty and Lord of hosts; that we may learn concerning God that he it is who is creator of heaven and earth and all the world, and maker of angels and men, and Lord of all, through whom all things exist and by whom all things are sustained; merciful, compassionate and very tender, good, just, the God of all — both of Jews and of Gentiles, and of those who believe. ([[Most High >> Bible:Ps 7:17]]; [[Lord of hosts >> Bible:Isa 6:3]]; [[God of Jews and Gentiles >> Bible:Rom 3:29]])

To those who believe he is as Father, for in the end of the times he opened up the covenant of adoption; ([[adoption >> Bible:Rom 8:15]]; [[Gal 4:5 >> Bible:Gal 4:5]]) but to the Jews as Lord and Lawgiver, for in the intermediate times, when humankind forgot God and revolted from him, he brought them into subjection by the Law, that they might learn that they had for Lord the maker and creator, who also gives the breath of life, and whom we ought to worship day and night; and to the Gentiles as maker and creator and almighty; and to all alike sustainer and nourisher and king and judge.

For none shall escape and be delivered from his judgment — neither Jew nor Gentile, nor believer that has sinned, nor angel: but they who now reject his goodness shall know his power in judgment, according to that which the blessed apostle says: ‘Not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance; but according to your hardness and impenitent heart you treasure up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who shall render to every one according to his works.’ ([[Rom 2:4-6 >> Bible:Rom 2:4-6]])

This is he who is called in the Law the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of the living; ([[Ex 3:6 >> Bible:Ex 3:6]]; [[Mt 22:32 >> Bible:Mt 22:32]]) although the sublimity and greatness of this God is unspeakable.

title: Seven heavens; sevenfold Spirit on the Son; menorah pattern
english: Now this world is encompassed by seven heavens, in which dwell powers and angels and archangels, doing service to God, the Almighty and Maker of all things: not as though he were in need, but that they may not be idle and unprofitable and ineffectual.

Wherefore also the Spirit of God is manifold in his indwelling, and in seven forms of service is he reckoned by the prophet Isaiah, as resting on the Son of God, that is the Word, in his coming as man. ‘The Spirit of God,’ he says, ‘shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and of might, the Spirit of knowledge and of godliness; the Spirit of the fear of God shall fill him.’ ([[Isa 11:2-3 >> Bible:Isa 11:2-3]])

Now the heaven which is first from above, and encompasses the rest, is that of wisdom; and the second from it, of understanding; and the third, of counsel; and the fourth, reckoned from above, is that of might; and the fifth, of knowledge; and the sixth, of godliness; and the seventh, this firmament of ours, is full of the fear of that Spirit which gives light to the heavens.

For, as the pattern of this, Moses received the seven-branched lampstand that shone continually in the holy place; for as a pattern of the heavens he received this service, according to that which the Word spoke unto him: ‘You shall make it according to all the pattern of the things which you have seen on the mountain.’ ([[Ex 25:40 >> Bible:Ex 25:40]]; [[Heb 8:5 >> Bible:Heb 8:5]]; [[seven lamps >> Bible:Ex 25:31-37]])
translator_notes: Independent English; seven-heavens cosmology as in Armenian/French.

title: Word and Wisdom glorify the Father; cherubim/seraphim; bounds of creation
english: Now this God is glorified by his Word who is his Son continually, and by the Holy Spirit who is the Wisdom of the Father of all; and the powers of these — namely of the Word and of Wisdom — which are called Cherubim and Seraphim, with unceasing voices glorify God; and every created thing that is in the heavens offers glory to God the Father of all. ([[holy, holy, holy >> Bible:Isa 6:3]]; [[Rev 4:8 >> Bible:Rev 4:8]])

He by his Word has created the whole world, and in the world are the angels; and to all the world he has given laws wherein each several thing should abide, and according to that which is determined by God should not pass their bounds, each fulfilling his appointed task. ([[set bounds >> Bible:Ps 104:9]]; [[Job 38:10-11 >> Bible:Job 38:10-11]]; [[Jer 5:22 >> Bible:Jer 5:22]])
translator_notes: Tip §§1–10. Independent English; Robinson/Wilson not copied. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew.
